text.ja: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS / FOUNDATIONS 分野を超えて使う 数値計算の基礎 誤差・安定性・散逸と分散・境界条件・分割法・幾何積分 全19章 · 19枚の図 · 38問の確認問題と解答 · 2026年11月24日版 PDFをダウンロード（A4・書籍版）旧PDF（2026-11-24版）小さな計算例のコードZIP共通の原稿JSON はじめに この教材は、特定の分野へ進む前に使える誤差・安定性・境界条件・時間積分の共通基礎です。微分積分と行列の初歩を前提にし、用いる記号は各章でも説明します。 まず直観を読み、定義と前提を確認し、手で追える計算例からコード・図へ進んでください。確認問題には短い解答を付けています。Webは解答を開いて読み、PDFでは同じ解答をそのまま確認できます。 少数の一次元問題と小さな行列を繰り返し使います。図の数が独立した物理問題の数という意味ではありません。新しい実物質計算、大規模走査、一般的な多次元ソルバーの性能評価は含めていません。 最初の風上法の粗い格子系列は設定した観測次数へ届きませんでした。入力・失敗結果を保存し、基準を変えずに細かい系列へ改訂しています。ここからも、観測次数と理論の関係を学べます。 想定読者：微分・積分と行列の初歩を学んだ初学者。特定の物理・工学分野の知識は前提にしない。 コード断片は配布ZIPのディレクトリで実行します。第19章のコマンドはシェルに入力します。 I 誤差を測り、結果を読む 近似と誤差の出どころ 絶対・相対誤差、丸め・打切り・反復誤差を区別し、桁数と精度を取り違えない。 誤差ノルム L1・L2・L∞ 連続ノルムと格子幅で重み付けした離散ノルムを使い分け、局所的な大誤差も見つける。 残差・条件数・後退誤差 問題の敏感さと解法の安定性を分け、小さい残差だけでは正確な解を保証しないと理解する。 整合性・打切り誤差・収束次数 局所誤差と大域誤差を区別し、Taylor展開と格子・時間刻みの細分化で精度を調べる。 II 安定性と数値不安定を理解する 安定性・収束とLaxの同値定理 適切に設定された線形初期値問題と整合する線形近似を対象に、決めたノルムでの一様な安定性と収束の関係を読む。 絶対安定性と安定領域 試験方程式 y'=λy と増幅関数 R(λΔt) を使い、時間刻みと増幅・減衰を結び付ける。 A安定性・L安定性・硬い問題 左半平面での安定性と非常に硬いモードの減衰を分け、安定でも時間精度は別と理解する。 von NeumannのFourier安定性解析 定係数・一様格子・周期または無限領域を基本として、波数ごとの増幅率を調べる。 CFL条件と依存領域 情報の伝わる速さと差分の届く範囲を結び付け、必要条件と十分条件を区別する。 数値散逸：振幅・ノルム・エネルギー 増幅率の絶対値から人工的な振幅減衰を読み、物理的な拡散・散逸と区別する。人工粘性の役割も学ぶ。 数値分散：位相速度・群速度・波形 増幅率の偏角から位相・伝播速度の誤差を読み、振幅が保たれても波形が崩れる理由を理解する。物理分散と区別する。 数値不安定と振動・発散の診断 誤差の増幅・発散を、安定だが振動的な解や物理的な不安定成長と区別し、原因を切り分ける。 III 初期条件・境界条件を扱う 初期条件とDirichlet・Neumann・Robin条件 値を与える、外向き法線微分を与える、両者を組み合わせる、という境界条件の意味を読む。 境界条件を離散化へ落とす 境界点・半格子・ゴースト点と法線の向きを図で確認し、境界だけの低次誤差を見つける。 適切性・純Neumannの互換条件と一意性 純Neumann問題の定数分の不定性と積分互換条件、平均値固定、境界を含む安定性を学ぶ。 IV 解法を組み合わせ、確かめる 線の方法と空間・時間誤差の切り分け 空間を離散化したODEと完全離散系を区別し、時間だけ・空間だけを変える比較を設計する。 Lie-Trotter分割とStrang分割 部分問題を順に解く合成と非可換性を学び、滑らかな条件での1次・2次、境界での次数低下を区別する。 シンプレクティック積分と長時間の振る舞い 調和振動子からHamilton系の位相空間を導入し、幾何構造を保つ時間積分とエネルギーの厳密保存を区別する。 小さな問題で検証する共通手順 解析解・製造解、誤差ノルム、収束、残差、保存量・エネルギー、境界誤差を一枚の手順にまとめる。 よく使う記号 h, Δx格子幅。節点かセル中心かも記す。Δt, n, T時間刻み、ステップ番号、比較する終時刻。u, U, e基準となる連続解、数値解、両者の差。λ, z, R(z)線形の増幅・減衰率、λΔt、時間積分の安定性関数。k, θ, G(θ)連続波数、無次元の格子波数kh、差分のFourier増幅率。κ(A)行列の条件数。熱の拡散係数κとは文脈を区別する。∂n, g外向き法線微分と境界の指定データ。q, p, H位置、運動量、Hamiltonian。一般の誤差次数pとは文脈を区別する。 参考資料と再現手順 Per-Olof Persson, Finite Difference Methods for PDEs 著者講義資料の差分・整合性・有限時間の一様安定性・Lax同値定理・熱の線の方法の関連箇所を参照。原著論文そのものや全文監査とは区別。 T. A. Driscoll and R. J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation: Stiffness 著者による教科書の半離散拡散、硬さ、線形化に関する該当箇所を参照。 Ernst Hairer, Lecture 2: Symplectic integrators (2010) 著者講義ノートPDF1-3ページの定義、シンプレクティックEuler、Störmer-Verlet、合成・分離形の箇所を参照。長時間の全定理や一般非線形問題を監査・再現したという意味ではない。 R. R. Rosales, Notes: von Neumann Stability Analysis (2022) 既存アトラスの関連資料として案内。既存の閲覧記録と区別し、この教材作成時の原文再読を主張しない。 教材の実行・制作範囲 Fixed small educational exercises. Intentional unstable/low-order controls and successful accurate-method checks have distinct meanings. Existing atlas scientific releases and their criteria are unchanged. 25単体テスト・34固定判定・15CSVをZIPの verify_release.py で再実行できます。意図的な不安定例は異常を検出する対照例です。
text.en: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS / FOUNDATIONS Numerical Foundations Across Disciplines Error, stability, dissipation and dispersion, boundary conditions, splitting, and geometric integration 19 chapters · 19 figures · 38 review questions with answers · 24 November 2026 Download the book PDF (US Letter)Previous PDF (24 November 2026)Small-example code ZIPShared manuscript JSON Introduction This course introduces error, stability, boundary conditions, and time integration before you move into a particular application. It assumes elementary calculus and matrices, and explains the notation again within each chapter. Start with the intuition, check the definitions and assumptions, and then work through the small calculations, code, and figures. Each review question has a short answer. On the Web, expand the answers to read them; the PDF displays those same answers in full. We reuse a small set of one-dimensional problems and small matrices. The number of figures is not the number of independent physical validation problems. The course does not include new real-material calculations, large parameter sweeps, or performance studies of general multidimensional solvers. The first coarse-grid sequence for the upwind method did not reach the prescribed observed order. We preserved its input and failed results and refined the grid sequence without changing the acceptance criterion. This also illustrates the relationship between observed and theoretical order. Audience: Beginners who have studied elementary differentiation, integration, and matrices. No background in a particular branch of physics or engineering is assumed. Run code snippets from the extracted ZIP directory. Enter the Chapter 19 commands in a shell rather than Python. I Measuring error and reading results Approximation and the sources of error Distinguish absolute and relative error, roundoff, truncation, and iteration error; do not confuse displayed digits with accuracy. Error norms: L1, L2, and L∞ Use continuous norms and grid-weighted discrete norms appropriately, and detect large localized errors. Residuals, conditioning, and backward error Separate sensitivity of the problem from stability of the algorithm, and understand why a small residual alone does not guarantee an accurate solution. Consistency, truncation error, and convergence order Distinguish local and global error, and investigate accuracy using Taylor expansions and refinement in space and time. II Understanding stability and numerical instability Stability, convergence, and the Lax equivalence theorem For a well-posed linear initial-value problem and a consistent linear approximation, relate uniform stability to convergence in a specified norm. Absolute stability and stability regions Use the test equation y′=λy and amplification function R(λΔt) to relate the time step to growth and decay. A-stability, L-stability, and stiff problems Separate stability over the left half-plane from damping of very stiff modes; accuracy remains a separate question. von Neumann Fourier stability analysis Examine amplification by wavenumber, primarily for constant coefficients on a uniform grid with periodic or infinite domains. CFL conditions and domains of dependence Connect information speed to the reach of a stencil, and distinguish necessary from sufficient conditions. Numerical dissipation: amplitude, norms, and energy Read artificial amplitude decay from the magnitude of the amplification factor, distinguish it from physical diffusion and dissipation, and understand the role of artificial viscosity. Numerical dispersion: phase speed, group speed, and waveforms Use the argument of amplification to examine phase and propagation-speed error, understand waveform distortion without amplitude loss, and distinguish physical dispersion. Diagnosing numerical instability, oscillation, and divergence Distinguish error amplification and divergence from stable oscillations and physical instability, and isolate their causes. III Working with initial and boundary conditions Initial conditions and Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin boundaries Understand prescribed values, outward normal derivatives, and linear combinations of the two. Turning boundary conditions into discrete equations Use boundary nodes, half cells, ghost points, and normal directions to identify errors caused by low-order boundary closures. Well-posedness, pure-Neumann compatibility, and uniqueness Understand the arbitrary constant, integral compatibility, mean-value gauge, and boundary-inclusive stability of a pure-Neumann problem. IV Combining methods and checking results The method of lines: separating space and time error Distinguish the spatially discrete ODE from the fully discrete system, and design comparisons that vary time or space separately. Lie-Trotter and Strang splitting Understand composition of subproblems and noncommutativity; distinguish first and second order under smooth conditions from boundary-induced order reduction. Symplectic integration and long-time behavior Introduce Hamiltonian phase space through the harmonic oscillator, and distinguish preservation of geometric structure from exact energy conservation. A common verification procedure using small problems Combine analytic and manufactured solutions, error norms, convergence, residuals, conserved quantities, energy budgets, and boundary error into one procedure. Frequently used notation h, ΔxGrid spacing. Also state whether the unknowns are located at nodes or cell centers.Δt, n, TTime step, step number, and the final time used for comparison.u, U, eReference continuous solution, numerical solution, and their difference.λ, z, R(z)Linear growth or decay rate, the product λΔt, and the stability function of a time integrator.k, θ, G(θ)Continuous wavenumber, dimensionless grid wavenumber kh, and the Fourier amplification factor of a discretization.κ(A)Matrix condition number. Distinguish it from a thermal diffusivity also denoted by κ.∂n, gOutward normal derivative and prescribed boundary data.q, p, HPosition, momentum, and Hamiltonian. Distinguish the momentum p from an error order also denoted by p. Using the examples Use Python 3.12 and only its standard library for the calculations. After extracting the shared code ZIP, run python verify_release.py from its directory. It reruns 25 calculation tests, 2 comparison tests, 34 fixed acceptance checks, and the comparison of 15 saved CSV files. No NumPy, network connection, randomness, or external solver is required. To inspect a fresh run, use python lab.py --input inputs.json --output my-results with a new or empty my-results directory. Read the individual criteria in my-results/result.json and compare its CSV files with the figures. The archive README and some provenance records are in Japanese; the English chapters and these instructions explain how to run and interpret the same unchanged code. The deliberately cancellation-sensitive derivative.csv is checked against an independent 80-digit Decimal Taylor reference and ULP-derived bounds, including checks of the floating-point sine and cosine assumptions at the fixed arguments. The other 14 CSV files retain relative tolerance 1e -9 and absolute tolerance 1e -10. This reproduction policy does not relax the original 34 scientific acceptance criteria. Regenerating plots additionally requires ReportLab 4.4.9 and Poppler; plot-byte equality is not required. References and reproduction Per-Olof Persson, Finite Difference Methods for PDEs Relevant sections of the author's lecture notes were consulted for finite differences, consistency, uniform finite-time stability, the Lax equivalence theorem, and the method of lines for heat diffusion. This is distinct from reading the original research paper or auditing the complete notes. T. A. Driscoll and R. J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation: Stiffness The relevant sections of the authors' textbook were consulted for semidiscrete diffusion, stiffness, and linearization. Ernst Hairer, Lecture 2: Symplectic integrators (2010) Pages 1-3 of the author's lecture-note PDF were consulted for the definition, symplectic Euler, Störmer-Verlet, composition, and separable systems. This does not claim an audit or reproduction of all long-time theorems or general nonlinear problems. R. R. Rosales, Notes: von Neumann Stability Analysis (2022) Provided as related reading already listed in the atlas. Earlier reading records are separate; we do not claim to have reread the original during preparation of this course. Scope of the computations and production Fixed small educational exercises. Intentional unstable/low-order controls and successful accurate-method checks have distinct meanings. Existing atlas scientific releases and their criteria are unchanged.
